---
name: slack-api
description: Read and write data in a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API. Use when the user wants to post, schedule, update, or delete Slack messages; reply in threads; list or create channels; read message history; invite members; look up users; search messages; add or remove emoji reactions; upload files; or fetch workspace info using a Slack bot or user token.
---

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/<method>`, JSON over HTTPS, bearer-token auth).

## Setup

1. Provide a token as the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable: a `xoxb-` bot token or `xoxp-` user token from a Slack app installed into the workspace. Never hard-code tokens or echo them in replies.
2. Confirm the app has the OAuth scopes for each method you call; see [references/api.md](references/api.md#2-tokens-and-oauth-scopes) for the scope map. A scope problem returns `missing_scope` with a `needed` field naming the scope.
3. Run a connectivity check first: `node scripts/slack_api.cjs api.test` (no scopes required).

## Quick start

Run the bundled helper from this skill's directory (or with its full path):

```bash
export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...

# Single call: pass a JSON object, or key=value pairs
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"#general","text":"Hello from Gemini CLI!"}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C1234567890","limit":10}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add channel=C1234567890 name=thumbsup ts=1712345678.123456

# Paginate through an entire list endpoint until next_cursor is empty
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel"}' --paginate channels
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.list '{}' --paginate members
```

The helper prints `Success: <JSON>` (truncated after ~4000 chars; use `--raw` for the full body) and exits 0. On failure it prints one clean line such as `Slack API error: missing_scope — missing scope "chat:write"` and exits 1. Flags: `--paginate <array-field>`, `--limit <n>`, `--max-pages <n>`, `--raw`.

## Core conventions

- Send every method as a `POST` to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` with a JSON body and `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`; all Web API methods accept this form.
- Success is `{"ok": true, ...}`; failure is `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>", ...}` (usually HTTP 200). Keep the `error` code verbatim when reporting to the user.
- Message `ts` values and `oldest`/`latest` bounds are Unix epoch seconds with fractional part (e.g. `1712345678.123456`) — always pass them as strings, never as JS numbers (precision loss breaks lookups).
- IDs: `C…`/`D…`/`G…` conversations, `U…` users, `T…` teams. Slack accepts `#channel-name` in several places (e.g. `chat.postMessage`), otherwise resolve names via `conversations.list`.
- Text supports mrkdwn (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|label>`, `<@U12345>`, `:wave:`); structured messages use `blocks` instead of `text`. Details in [references/api.md](references/api.md#6-message-formatting).
- Paginate: list endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; request pages of ≤200 with `cursor` until it comes back empty. Never assume a single call returns everything.

## Typical flows

- **Send or reply**: `chat.postMessage` with `channel`, `text` and/or `blocks`; add `thread_ts` to reply inside a thread.
- **Read a channel**: `conversations.list` → pick `channel.id` → `conversations.history`; follow thread replies with `conversations.replies` on the parent `ts`.
- **DM a user**: `users.lookupByEmail` → `conversations.open` → `chat.postMessage` to the returned channel id.
- **Find past messages**: `search.messages` with query filters such as `in:#general after:2024-01-01`.
- **Create and populate a channel**: `conversations.create` then `conversations.invite`.
- **Send a file**: use the two-step v2 flow (`files.getUploadURLExternal` + binary upload + `files.completeUploadExternal`); see [references/api.md](references/api.md#8-files).

Payload shapes, response essentials, and scopes for every method are cataloged in [references/api.md](references/api.md#5-method-catalog) — read it before composing any call you are unsure about.

## Error handling

Retry transient failures (`ratelimited`/HTTP 429, `internal_error`, `fatal_error`) up to 3 times with exponential backoff, honoring `Retry-After`. Do not blindly retry write methods on ambiguous failures: a retried `chat.postMessage` can duplicate a message. Common codes and fixes are in [references/api.md](references/api.md#10-error-codes-and-rate-limits).

# Slack Web API Reference

Table of contents:
1. [Helper usage](#1-helper-usage)
2. [Tokens and OAuth scopes](#2-tokens-and-oauth-scopes)
3. [Pagination and limits](#3-pagination-and-limits)
4. [Timestamps and IDs](#4-timestamps-and-ids)
5. [Method catalog](#5-method-catalog)
6. [Message formatting (mrkdwn)](#6-message-formatting-mrkdwn)
7. [Block Kit](#7-block-kit)
8. [Files](#8-files)
9. [Diagnostics](#9-diagnostics)
10. [Error codes and rate limits](#10-error-codes-and-rate-limits)

## 1. Helper usage

`node scripts/slack_api.cjs <method> [args] [flags]` with `SLACK_TOKEN` exported.

- **args**: one JSON object (`'{"channel":"C1","text":"hi"}'`) and/or any number of `key=value` pairs (`channel=C1 text=hi`). Values are parsed as JSON when possible; keys `ts`, `thread_ts`, `oldest`, `latest` keep decimal values as strings so timestamp precision is preserved.
- **flags**:
  - `--paginate <field>` — follow `response_metadata.next_cursor` until it is empty, collecting the array field across pages (e.g. `channels`, `members`, `messages`, `users`).
  - `--limit <n>` — page size for paginated calls (default 200).
  - `--max-pages <n>` — safety cap on total pages (default 200).
  - `--raw` — print the full JSON without truncation (default truncates at ~4000 chars).
- **Exit codes**: 0 success; 1 Slack/network error (reason printed on stderr); 2 usage error.
- One-off file uploads need a raw binary `POST` step, so use the flow in [Files](#8-files) rather than this JSON helper.

## 2. Tokens and OAuth scopes

Token types: `xoxb-` bot token (acts as the app; recommended) and `xoxp-` user token (acts as a user). Scopes are granted to the app at install time; changing scopes requires reinstalling the app.

Common scopes by capability:

| Capability | Scopes |
|---|---|
| Send/edit/delete/schedule messages | `chat:write` (+ `chat:write.public` to post to public channels the app has not joined) |
| Read public channel history | `channels:history`, `channels:read` |
| Read private channel (group) history | `groups:history`, `groups:read` |
| Read DM / group-DM history | `im:history`, `im:read`, `mpim:history`, `mpim:read` |
| Manage public channels (create/invite/archive/topic) | `channels:manage` (+ `channels:join` to join) |
| Manage private channels | `groups:write` |
| Open DMs | `im:write` (single) / `mpim:write` (group) |
| Users | `users:read` (+ `users:read.email` for emails, `users:write`) |
| Search | `search:read` |
| Emoji reactions | `reactions:read`, `reactions:write` |
| Files | `files:write` |
| Workspace info | `team:read` |

## 3. Pagination and limits

- List endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor` and repeat until it is empty. `conversations.history` additionally returns `has_more`.
- Default page size is 100 and caps vary by method (commonly 200). Request 100–200 items per page and always paginate instead of expecting huge one-shot pages.
- Helper field names for `--paginate`: `conversations.list` → `channels`, `users.list` → `members`, `conversations.members` → `members`, `conversations.history`/`replies` → `messages`.
- `search.messages` does **not** use cursors — page with `count` (≤100) and `page` (≤100) instead.

## 4. Timestamps and IDs

- Conversation ids start with `C` (public/private channels), `D` (DMs), `G` (private groups/mpims); users `U`; teams `T`.
- Timestamps are Unix epoch seconds with up to 6 fractional digits (`1712345678.123456`). Treat them as opaque strings end to end; converting to a JS/Python number can lose precision and produce `invalid_ts`.
- Search date filters use `YYYY-MM-DD` (`after:2024-01-01`).

## 5. Method catalog

### Messaging
- `chat.postMessage` — send a message. Key params: `channel` (id or `#name`), `text` and/or `blocks` (at least one), `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn` (default true), `link_names` (1 to linkify names), `reply_broadcast` (also post a thread reply to the channel), `unfurl_links`/`unfurl_media`. Scope: `chat:write`. Returns `ts`, `channel`, `message`.
- `chat.postEphemeral` — message visible only to `user`; params as above plus `user`. Scope `chat:write`.
- `chat.update` — edit an existing message: `channel`, `ts`, new `text`/`blocks`. Scope `chat:write`. Only messages the same identity (bot or user) posted can be edited.
- `chat.delete` — delete: `channel`, `ts`. Scope `chat:write`. Only own messages.
- `chat.scheduleMessage` — schedule a future message with `post_at` (Unix seconds, up to ~120 days ahead; paid plans). Returns `scheduled_message_id`; cancel with `chat.deleteScheduledMessage` (`channel`, `scheduled_message_id`). Scope `chat:write`.

### Conversations (channels, DMs, groups)
Channel objects carry `id`, `name`, `is_channel`, `is_private`, `is_im`, `is_mpim`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `num_members`, `topic`, `purpose`.

- `conversations.list` — paginated. Params: `types` (comma list; default `public_channel`; add `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im` as needed), `exclude_archived`, `cursor`, `limit`. Returns `channels[]`. Scopes: read scope matching each requested type.
- `conversations.info` — one channel: `channel`, `include_num_members`. Scopes: matching read scope.
- `conversations.history` — `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` (string timestamps), `inclusive`. Returns `messages[]`, `has_more`. Scopes: `channels:history` (public), `groups:history` (private), `im:history`/`mpim:history` (DMs).
- `conversations.replies` — all messages in a thread: `channel`, `ts` (parent). Scopes: same as history.
- `conversations.members` — paginated member user-ids: `members[]`. Scopes: `channels:read`/`groups:read`.
- `conversations.open` — get or create a DM/mpim: `users` (single id → DM; comma list → mpim). Returns `channel.id`; pass that to `chat.postMessage`. Scopes: `im:write`/`mpim:write`.
- `conversations.create` — `name` (no `#`), `is_private` (default false). Returns the new channel. Scopes: `channels:manage` (public) / `groups:write` (private).
- `conversations.rename` — `channel`, `name`. Same scopes as create.
- `conversations.invite` — `channel`, `users` (comma-separated ids). Scopes: `channels:manage`/`groups:write`. Possible errors: `already_in_channel`, `cant_invite_self`.
- `conversations.join` — join a public channel: `channel`. Scope: `channels:join`.
- `conversations.leave`, `conversations.archive`, `conversations.unarchive` — `channel`. Scopes: manage/write as above.
- `conversations.setTopic` — `channel`, `topic`; `conversations.setPurpose` — `channel`, `purpose`. Scopes: manage/write.
- `conversations.kick` — remove `user` from `channel`. Scopes: manage/write.

### Users
- `users.list` — paginated `members[]` with profiles (`profile.email` requires `users:read.email`), `is_bot`, `deleted`. Scope: `users:read`.
- `users.info` — `user` id → `user` object. Scope: `users:read`.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — `email` → `user`. Scope: `users:read.email`.
- `users.conversations` — paginated conversations a user is in; params like `conversations.list`. Scope: channel-type read scopes + `users:read`.

### Search
- `search.messages` — `query` with filters: `in:#channel`, `from:@user`, `after:YYYY-MM-DD`, `before:YYYY-MM-DD`, `has:link`. Returns `messages.matches[]`, each with `ts`, `channel` (id + name), `user`, `text`, `permalink`, `blocks`. Scope: `search:read`. Page with `count`/`page` (not cursors).

### Reactions
- `reactions.add` — `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `thumbsup`), `timestamp` (string). Scope: `reactions:write`. `no_reaction` means the emoji does not exist.
- `reactions.remove` — same params. Scope: `reactions:write`.
- `reactions.get` — `channel`, `timestamp` → message with `reactions[]` (`name`, `count`, `users[]`). Scope: `reactions:read`.

### Workspace and diagnostics
- `team.info` — `team` with `id`, `name`, `domain`. Scope: `team:read`.
- `auth.test` — validates the token and shows `user_id`, `team_id`, `url`. No scopes.
- `api.test` — connectivity check (no auth needed); echoes any `args` you pass.

## 6. Message formatting (mrkdwn)

| Want | Write |
|---|---|
| Bold | `*text*` |
| Italic | `_text_` |
| Strikethrough | `~text~` |
| Inline code | `` `code` `` |
| Preformatted block | ` ```code``` ` |
| Link with label | `<https://example.com|label>` |
| Mention a user | `<@U12345>` or `<@U12345|Label>` |
| Mention a channel | `<#C12345>` or `<#C12345|label>` |
| Emoji | `:wave:` |
| Broadcast | `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>` |

mrkdwn is parsed in `text` by default (`mrkdwn: true`); `blocks` text is plain unless the block uses `"type": "mrkdwn"`.

## 7. Block Kit

Use `blocks` for structured messages (buttons, inputs, layouts). Minimal example:

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Hello* <@U12345>" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Approve", "emoji": true },
          "value": "approve_1", "action_id": "approve" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Common block types: `section`, `divider`, `actions`, `context`, `header`, `input`, `image`, `file`. A plain-text message with `text` and a Block Kit message with `blocks` are separate messages (you cannot mix one `text` field into a `blocks` payload; post either `text` or `blocks`, or both as parallel top-level fields where the text serves as fallback). Interactive elements (buttons, modals) require the Events/Interactivity API, which is outside the Web API scope of this skill.

## 8. Files

Use the current two-step upload flow (the old one-step `files.upload` is deprecated). Scopes: `files:write`.

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename`, `length` (bytes), optional `alt_txt`, `snippet_type` → returns `upload_url` and `file_id`.
2. Upload the raw bytes to `upload_url` (not `slack.com/api`):

```js
const res = await fetch(uploadURL, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'image/png' }, // match the file's MIME type
  body: fileBuffer,                          // raw bytes, not JSON
});
```

3. `files.completeUploadExternal` with `{ "files": [{ "id": file_id, "title": "optional" }], "channel_id": "C123", "initial_comment": "optional" }` → returns the shared `file` object.

This is a low-freedom sequence: write a short one-off script that performs all three steps and prints the resulting `file` summary; verify the file id and final `ok` before reporting success.

## 9. Diagnostics

Order of checks when something fails:
1. `api.test` — is the network/base URL reachable?
2. `auth.test` — is `SLACK_TOKEN` valid and is the app installed in the workspace?
3. Re-run the failing call and read the exact `error` code (and `response_metadata.messages` for `invalid_arguments`).
4. `missing_scope`/`not_authorized` → the app needs the scope named in `needed`; scope changes require reinstalling the app, so tell the user to reinstall it after updating scopes.

## 10. Error codes and rate limits

| Code | Meaning / fix |
|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Token missing, mistyped, or revoked — re-export `SLACK_TOKEN`. |
| `account_inactive` | User token revoked/deactivated. |
| `missing_scope` / `not_authorized` | Token lacks permission; the `needed` field names the scope. |
| `channel_not_found` / `user_not_found` | Bad id, or the app is not in that channel — join or invite first. |
| `not_in_channel` | App must join/invite before acting on a channel. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive first. |
| `invalid_ts` / `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` malformed or corrupted by float conversion — pass timestamps as strings. |
| `msg_too_long` | Over 40,000 chars — split into multiple messages. |
| `already_in_channel`, `already_archived`, `name_taken`, `no_reaction` | Idempotent/state conflicts — report and stop rather than retry. |
| `invalid_arguments` | Check `response_metadata.messages` for field-level errors. |
| `ratelimited` (HTTP 429) | Slow down; respect `Retry-After` seconds. |
| `internal_error` / `fatal_error` | Transient — safe to retry with backoff. |

Rate limiting is per-method and tiered (most methods sustain ~1+ request/second; search and a few others are stricter). Pace long pagination runs (small sleeps between pages), retry 429/`internal_error` with jittered exponential backoff (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s, up to 3 tries), and never auto-retry after ambiguous failures on write methods that can duplicate side effects.

---
name: slack-api
description: Work with the Slack Web API to post messages, read conversations, manage channels, upload files, and search workspace data. Use when a task involves Slack automation such as sending notifications or alerts, retrieving channel history, resolving channel or user IDs, replying in threads, or polling workspace activity.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Slack exposes an HTTP Web API at `https://slack.com/api`. Every endpoint returns JSON and reports success with an `ok` field (`ok: true` or `ok: false`). This skill covers the operations an agent most often needs: sending and managing messages, reading conversations, resolving IDs, uploading files, and searching.

## Prerequisites

- Access token: a bot token (`xoxb-...`) for bot actions or a user token (`xoxp-...`) for user-scoped actions. Some workspaces also use workspace tokens (`xwok-...`).
- Never hardcode tokens. Read them from an environment variable such as `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` or `SLACK_TOKEN`.
- Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Verify the token's scopes cover the operation. A missing scope returns `ok: false` with `error: missing_scope`. Common scopes: `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `users:read`, `files:write`, `search:read`.

## Calling the API

Use HTTP POST with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for simple fields, or `application/json; charset=utf-8` when the payload contains rich `blocks` JSON (JSON bodies are required for `files.upload_v2`). GET with query parameters also works on read endpoints.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C1234567890", "text": "Hello from an agent"}'
```

Always inspect the JSON result:

- `{"ok": true, ...}` — success; use returned IDs (`ts`, `channel`, `file.id`) for follow-ups.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "invalid_auth"}` — token invalid; stop and report.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "not_in_channel"}` — bot must join the channel first via `conversations.join`.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found"}` — the channel argument was not a valid channel ID.
- HTTP 429 with `{"ok": false, "error": "rate_limited"}` — wait for the `Retry-After` header seconds and retry once.

## Resolving IDs

Endpoints expect IDs, not display names. `#general` or `general` will fail on most endpoints. Resolve first:

- **Channel ID from name**: `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel` and `limit=200`, paginating with `cursor`, then match `name` or `name_normalized`. `channels.list` and `groups.list` are legacy aliases.
- **User ID from email**: `users.lookupByEmail` with `email=...` returns `user.id`.
- **User ID from name**: `users.list` (paginate with `cursor`) and match `name` or `profile.display_name`.

## Sending and Managing Messages

### Post a message

`chat.postMessage` with `channel` (channel, user, or conversation ID), `text`, and optional `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `username`/`icon_emoji` (bot tokens only), and `link_names`.

### Reply in a thread

Pass `thread_ts` equal to the parent message's `ts`. Replies without `thread_ts` start new messages. To fetch a thread, use `conversations.replies` with `channel` and `ts`.

### Update and delete

- `chat.update` — requires `channel` and `ts` of the original message; supports `text` and `blocks`.
- `chat.delete` — requires `channel` and `ts`. Deletes are irreversible; prefer `chat.postMessage` with a corrective message if unsure.
- `chat.postEphemeral` — send a message only a specific user sees (`user` field required).

## Reading Conversations

- `conversations.history` — fetch messages from a channel with `channel`, `limit` (1–999), `oldest`/`latest` (Unix timestamps or `ts` values), and `inclusive`.
- `conversations.replies` — fetch a thread by `channel` + `ts`.
- `conversations.info` — metadata for one channel.
- `conversations.members` — list member user IDs of a channel.

Paginate every list-style call: when `response_metadata.next_cursor` is non-empty, repeat the call adding `cursor=<next_cursor>`. Do not assume `limit` returns everything.

## Users and Presence

- `users.info` with `user` — profile, timezone, status, and `is_bot`.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — fastest way to get a user ID.
- `users.list` — all workspace users; paginate.
- `users.getPresence` with `user` — `active`/`away` presence.

## Uploading Files

- `files.upload_v2` (preferred) with `channel_id`, `content` or `file`/`filename`/`filetype`, and optional `initial_comment`. Returns `file.id`; the file appears in the channel when `channel_id` is supplied.
- `files.upload` (legacy) — for a single channel; JSON body required.
- `files.sharedPublicURL` — generate a public link for a file that already has `permalink_public` enabled.

## Searching

- `search.messages` with `query` — returns matching messages plus `permalink` and channel/thread context.
- `search.files` with `query` — returns matching files.
- Query syntax supports `from:@user`, `in:#channel`, `before:/after:` datestamps, and quoted phrases.
- User-token scopes (`search:read`) are required; bot tokens cannot search by default.

## Message Formatting

- **mrkdwn** in `text`: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `~strike~`, `<https://example.com|Link text>`, `@user`, `#channel`. Escape literal `&`, `<`, `>`.
- **Blocks**: `blocks` (JSON array) renders a rich layout (section, header, divider, context, actions) and is the recommended way to compose professional messages. When `blocks` is present, also provide a plain-text `text` fallback for notifications and accessibility.
- Line breaks in `text` are honored; use `\n` in JSON strings.

## Recommended Workflow

1. Confirm the target: workspace, channel or DM, user, and desired content.
2. Resolve channel/user IDs before messaging.
3. For one-off notifications, post a message with `blocks` plus a `text` fallback and report the resulting `ts` and permalink (`https://<workspace>.slack.com/archives/<channel>/p<ts-without-dot>`).
4. For reads that may exceed one page, always loop on `next_cursor`.
5. On failure, read `error` and act on it (join channel, fix scope, wait `Retry-After`) rather than retrying blindly.
6. Never fabricate a token, channel ID, message timestamp, or API success. If a call was not actually executed, say so.

arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Read and write data in a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API. Use when the user wants to post, schedule, update, or delete Slack messages; reply in threads; list or create channels; read message history; invite members; look up users; search messages; add or remove emoji reactions; upload files; or fetch workspace info using a Slack bot or user token.
---

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/<method>`, JSON over HTTPS, bearer-token auth).

## Setup

1. Provide a token as the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable: a `xoxb-` bot token or `xoxp-` user token from a Slack app installed into the workspace. Never hard-code tokens or echo them in replies.
2. Confirm the app has the OAuth scopes for each method you call; see [references/api.md](references/api.md#2-tokens-and-oauth-scopes) for the scope map. A scope problem returns `missing_scope` with a `needed` field naming the scope.
3. Run a connectivity check first: `node scripts/slack_api.cjs api.test` (no scopes required).

## Quick start

Run the bundled helper from this skill's directory (or with its full path):

```bash
export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...

# Single call: pass a JSON object, or key=value pairs
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"#general","text":"Hello from Gemini CLI!"}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C1234567890","limit":10}'
node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add channel=C1234567890 name=thumbsup ts=1712345678.123456

# Paginate through an entire list endpoint until next_cursor is empty
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel"}' --paginate channels
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.list '{}' --paginate members
```

The helper prints `Success: <JSON>` (truncated after ~4000 chars; use `--raw` for the full body) and exits 0. On failure it prints one clean line such as `Slack API error: missing_scope — missing scope "chat:write"` and exits 1. Flags: `--paginate <array-field>`, `--limit <n>`, `--max-pages <n>`, `--raw`.

## Core conventions

- Send every method as a `POST` to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` with a JSON body and `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`; all Web API methods accept this form.
- Success is `{"ok": true, ...}`; failure is `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>", ...}` (usually HTTP 200). Keep the `error` code verbatim when reporting to the user.
- Message `ts` values and `oldest`/`latest` bounds are Unix epoch seconds with fractional part (e.g. `1712345678.123456`) — always pass them as strings, never as JS numbers (precision loss breaks lookups).
- IDs: `C…`/`D…`/`G…` conversations, `U…` users, `T…` teams. Slack accepts `#channel-name` in several places (e.g. `chat.postMessage`), otherwise resolve names via `conversations.list`.
- Text supports mrkdwn (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|label>`, `<@U12345>`, `:wave:`); structured messages use `blocks` instead of `text`. Details in [references/api.md](references/api.md#6-message-formatting).
- Paginate: list endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; request pages of ≤200 with `cursor` until it comes back empty. Never assume a single call returns everything.

## Typical flows

- **Send or reply**: `chat.postMessage` with `channel`, `text` and/or `blocks`; add `thread_ts` to reply inside a thread.
- **Read a channel**: `conversations.list` → pick `channel.id` → `conversations.history`; follow thread replies with `conversations.replies` on the parent `ts`.
- **DM a user**: `users.lookupByEmail` → `conversations.open` → `chat.postMessage` to the returned channel id.
- **Find past messages**: `search.messages` with query filters such as `in:#general after:2024-01-01`.
- **Create and populate a channel**: `conversations.create` then `conversations.invite`.
- **Send a file**: use the two-step v2 flow (`files.getUploadURLExternal` + binary upload + `files.completeUploadExternal`); see [references/api.md](references/api.md#8-files).

Payload shapes, response essentials, and scopes for every method are cataloged in [references/api.md](references/api.md#5-method-catalog) — read it before composing any call you are unsure about.

## Error handling

Retry transient failures (`ratelimited`/HTTP 429, `internal_error`, `fatal_error`) up to 3 times with exponential backoff, honoring `Retry-After`. Do not blindly retry write methods on ambiguous failures: a retried `chat.postMessage` can duplicate a message. Common codes and fixes are in [references/api.md](references/api.md#10-error-codes-and-rate-limits).

# Slack Web API Reference

Table of contents:
1. [Helper usage](#1-helper-usage)
2. [Tokens and OAuth scopes](#2-tokens-and-oauth-scopes)
3. [Pagination and limits](#3-pagination-and-limits)
4. [Timestamps and IDs](#4-timestamps-and-ids)
5. [Method catalog](#5-method-catalog)
6. [Message formatting (mrkdwn)](#6-message-formatting-mrkdwn)
7. [Block Kit](#7-block-kit)
8. [Files](#8-files)
9. [Diagnostics](#9-diagnostics)
10. [Error codes and rate limits](#10-error-codes-and-rate-limits)

## 1. Helper usage

`node scripts/slack_api.cjs <method> [args] [flags]` with `SLACK_TOKEN` exported.

- **args**: one JSON object (`'{"channel":"C1","text":"hi"}'`) and/or any number of `key=value` pairs (`channel=C1 text=hi`). Values are parsed as JSON when possible; keys `ts`, `thread_ts`, `oldest`, `latest` keep decimal values as strings so timestamp precision is preserved.
- **flags**:
  - `--paginate <field>` — follow `response_metadata.next_cursor` until it is empty, collecting the array field across pages (e.g. `channels`, `members`, `messages`, `users`).
  - `--limit <n>` — page size for paginated calls (default 200).
  - `--max-pages <n>` — safety cap on total pages (default 200).
  - `--raw` — print the full JSON without truncation (default truncates at ~4000 chars).
- **Exit codes**: 0 success; 1 Slack/network error (reason printed on stderr); 2 usage error.
- One-off file uploads need a raw binary `POST` step, so use the flow in [Files](#8-files) rather than this JSON helper.

## 2. Tokens and OAuth scopes

Token types: `xoxb-` bot token (acts as the app; recommended) and `xoxp-` user token (acts as a user). Scopes are granted to the app at install time; changing scopes requires reinstalling the app.

Common scopes by capability:

| Capability | Scopes |
|---|---|
| Send/edit/delete/schedule messages | `chat:write` (+ `chat:write.public` to post to public channels the app has not joined) |
| Read public channel history | `channels:history`, `channels:read` |
| Read private channel (group) history | `groups:history`, `groups:read` |
| Read DM / group-DM history | `im:history`, `im:read`, `mpim:history`, `mpim:read` |
| Manage public channels (create/invite/archive/topic) | `channels:manage` (+ `channels:join` to join) |
| Manage private channels | `groups:write` |
| Open DMs | `im:write` (single) / `mpim:write` (group) |
| Users | `users:read` (+ `users:read.email` for emails, `users:write`) |
| Search | `search:read` |
| Emoji reactions | `reactions:read`, `reactions:write` |
| Files | `files:write` |
| Workspace info | `team:read` |

## 3. Pagination and limits

- List endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor` and repeat until it is empty. `conversations.history` additionally returns `has_more`.
- Default page size is 100 and caps vary by method (commonly 200). Request 100–200 items per page and always paginate instead of expecting huge one-shot pages.
- Helper field names for `--paginate`: `conversations.list` → `channels`, `users.list` → `members`, `conversations.members` → `members`, `conversations.history`/`replies` → `messages`.
- `search.messages` does **not** use cursors — page with `count` (≤100) and `page` (≤100) instead.

## 4. Timestamps and IDs

- Conversation ids start with `C` (public/private channels), `D` (DMs), `G` (private groups/mpims); users `U`; teams `T`.
- Timestamps are Unix epoch seconds with up to 6 fractional digits (`1712345678.123456`). Treat them as opaque strings end to end; converting to a JS/Python number can lose precision and produce `invalid_ts`.
- Search date filters use `YYYY-MM-DD` (`after:2024-01-01`).

## 5. Method catalog

### Messaging
- `chat.postMessage` — send a message. Key params: `channel` (id or `#name`), `text` and/or `blocks` (at least one), `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn` (default true), `link_names` (1 to linkify names), `reply_broadcast` (also post a thread reply to the channel), `unfurl_links`/`unfurl_media`. Scope: `chat:write`. Returns `ts`, `channel`, `message`.
- `chat.postEphemeral` — message visible only to `user`; params as above plus `user`. Scope `chat:write`.
- `chat.update` — edit an existing message: `channel`, `ts`, new `text`/`blocks`. Scope `chat:write`. Only messages the same identity (bot or user) posted can be edited.
- `chat.delete` — delete: `channel`, `ts`. Scope `chat:write`. Only own messages.
- `chat.scheduleMessage` — schedule a future message with `post_at` (Unix seconds, up to ~120 days ahead; paid plans). Returns `scheduled_message_id`; cancel with `chat.deleteScheduledMessage` (`channel`, `scheduled_message_id`). Scope `chat:write`.

### Conversations (channels, DMs, groups)
Channel objects carry `id`, `name`, `is_channel`, `is_private`, `is_im`, `is_mpim`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `num_members`, `topic`, `purpose`.

- `conversations.list` — paginated. Params: `types` (comma list; default `public_channel`; add `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im` as needed), `exclude_archived`, `cursor`, `limit`. Returns `channels[]`. Scopes: read scope matching each requested type.
- `conversations.info` — one channel: `channel`, `include_num_members`. Scopes: matching read scope.
- `conversations.history` — `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` (string timestamps), `inclusive`. Returns `messages[]`, `has_more`. Scopes: `channels:history` (public), `groups:history` (private), `im:history`/`mpim:history` (DMs).
- `conversations.replies` — all messages in a thread: `channel`, `ts` (parent). Scopes: same as history.
- `conversations.members` — paginated member user-ids: `members[]`. Scopes: `channels:read`/`groups:read`.
- `conversations.open` — get or create a DM/mpim: `users` (single id → DM; comma list → mpim). Returns `channel.id`; pass that to `chat.postMessage`. Scopes: `im:write`/`mpim:write`.
- `conversations.create` — `name` (no `#`), `is_private` (default false). Returns the new channel. Scopes: `channels:manage` (public) / `groups:write` (private).
- `conversations.rename` — `channel`, `name`. Same scopes as create.
- `conversations.invite` — `channel`, `users` (comma-separated ids). Scopes: `channels:manage`/`groups:write`. Possible errors: `already_in_channel`, `cant_invite_self`.
- `conversations.join` — join a public channel: `channel`. Scope: `channels:join`.
- `conversations.leave`, `conversations.archive`, `conversations.unarchive` — `channel`. Scopes: manage/write as above.
- `conversations.setTopic` — `channel`, `topic`; `conversations.setPurpose` — `channel`, `purpose`. Scopes: manage/write.
- `conversations.kick` — remove `user` from `channel`. Scopes: manage/write.

### Users
- `users.list` — paginated `members[]` with profiles (`profile.email` requires `users:read.email`), `is_bot`, `deleted`. Scope: `users:read`.
- `users.info` — `user` id → `user` object. Scope: `users:read`.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — `email` → `user`. Scope: `users:read.email`.
- `users.conversations` — paginated conversations a user is in; params like `conversations.list`. Scope: channel-type read scopes + `users:read`.

### Search
- `search.messages` — `query` with filters: `in:#channel`, `from:@user`, `after:YYYY-MM-DD`, `before:YYYY-MM-DD`, `has:link`. Returns `messages.matches[]`, each with `ts`, `channel` (id + name), `user`, `text`, `permalink`, `blocks`. Scope: `search:read`. Page with `count`/`page` (not cursors).

### Reactions
- `reactions.add` — `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `thumbsup`), `timestamp` (string). Scope: `reactions:write`. `no_reaction` means the emoji does not exist.
- `reactions.remove` — same params. Scope: `reactions:write`.
- `reactions.get` — `channel`, `timestamp` → message with `reactions[]` (`name`, `count`, `users[]`). Scope: `reactions:read`.

### Workspace and diagnostics
- `team.info` — `team` with `id`, `name`, `domain`. Scope: `team:read`.
- `auth.test` — validates the token and shows `user_id`, `team_id`, `url`. No scopes.
- `api.test` — connectivity check (no auth needed); echoes any `args` you pass.

## 6. Message formatting (mrkdwn)

| Want | Write |
|---|---|
| Bold | `*text*` |
| Italic | `_text_` |
| Strikethrough | `~text~` |
| Inline code | `` `code` `` |
| Preformatted block | ` ```code``` ` |
| Link with label | `<https://example.com|label>` |
| Mention a user | `<@U12345>` or `<@U12345|Label>` |
| Mention a channel | `<#C12345>` or `<#C12345|label>` |
| Emoji | `:wave:` |
| Broadcast | `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>` |

mrkdwn is parsed in `text` by default (`mrkdwn: true`); `blocks` text is plain unless the block uses `"type": "mrkdwn"`.

## 7. Block Kit

Use `blocks` for structured messages (buttons, inputs, layouts). Minimal example:

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Hello* <@U12345>" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Approve", "emoji": true },
          "value": "approve_1", "action_id": "approve" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Common block types: `section`, `divider`, `actions`, `context`, `header`, `input`, `image`, `file`. A plain-text message with `text` and a Block Kit message with `blocks` are separate messages (you cannot mix one `text` field into a `blocks` payload; post either `text` or `blocks`, or both as parallel top-level fields where the text serves as fallback). Interactive elements (buttons, modals) require the Events/Interactivity API, which is outside the Web API scope of this skill.

## 8. Files

Use the current two-step upload flow (the old one-step `files.upload` is deprecated). Scopes: `files:write`.

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename`, `length` (bytes), optional `alt_txt`, `snippet_type` → returns `upload_url` and `file_id`.
2. Upload the raw bytes to `upload_url` (not `slack.com/api`):

```js
const res = await fetch(uploadURL, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'image/png' }, // match the file's MIME type
  body: fileBuffer,                          // raw bytes, not JSON
});
```

3. `files.completeUploadExternal` with `{ "files": [{ "id": file_id, "title": "optional" }], "channel_id": "C123", "initial_comment": "optional" }` → returns the shared `file` object.

This is a low-freedom sequence: write a short one-off script that performs all three steps and prints the resulting `file` summary; verify the file id and final `ok` before reporting success.

## 9. Diagnostics

Order of checks when something fails:
1. `api.test` — is the network/base URL reachable?
2. `auth.test` — is `SLACK_TOKEN` valid and is the app installed in the workspace?
3. Re-run the failing call and read the exact `error` code (and `response_metadata.messages` for `invalid_arguments`).
4. `missing_scope`/`not_authorized` → the app needs the scope named in `needed`; scope changes require reinstalling the app, so tell the user to reinstall it after updating scopes.

## 10. Error codes and rate limits

| Code | Meaning / fix |
|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Token missing, mistyped, or revoked — re-export `SLACK_TOKEN`. |
| `account_inactive` | User token revoked/deactivated. |
| `missing_scope` / `not_authorized` | Token lacks permission; the `needed` field names the scope. |
| `channel_not_found` / `user_not_found` | Bad id, or the app is not in that channel — join or invite first. |
| `not_in_channel` | App must join/invite before acting on a channel. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive first. |
| `invalid_ts` / `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` malformed or corrupted by float conversion — pass timestamps as strings. |
| `msg_too_long` | Over 40,000 chars — split into multiple messages. |
| `already_in_channel`, `already_archived`, `name_taken`, `no_reaction` | Idempotent/state conflicts — report and stop rather than retry. |
| `invalid_arguments` | Check `response_metadata.messages` for field-level errors. |
| `ratelimited` (HTTP 429) | Slow down; respect `Retry-After` seconds. |
| `internal_error` / `fatal_error` | Transient — safe to retry with backoff. |

Rate limiting is per-method and tiered (most methods sustain ~1+ request/second; search and a few others are stricter). Pace long pagination runs (small sleeps between pages), retry 429/`internal_error` with jittered exponential backoff (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s, up to 3 tries), and never auto-retry after ambiguous failures on write methods that can duplicate side effects.

---
name: slack-api
description: Work with the Slack Web API to post messages, read conversations, manage channels, upload files, and search workspace data. Use when a task involves Slack automation such as sending notifications or alerts, retrieving channel history, resolving channel or user IDs, replying in threads, or polling workspace activity.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Slack exposes an HTTP Web API at `https://slack.com/api`. Every endpoint returns JSON and reports success with an `ok` field (`ok: true` or `ok: false`). This skill covers the operations an agent most often needs: sending and managing messages, reading conversations, resolving IDs, uploading files, and searching.

## Prerequisites

- Access token: a bot token (`xoxb-...`) for bot actions or a user token (`xoxp-...`) for user-scoped actions. Some workspaces also use workspace tokens (`xwok-...`).
- Never hardcode tokens. Read them from an environment variable such as `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` or `SLACK_TOKEN`.
- Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Verify the token's scopes cover the operation. A missing scope returns `ok: false` with `error: missing_scope`. Common scopes: `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `users:read`, `files:write`, `search:read`.

## Calling the API

Use HTTP POST with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for simple fields, or `application/json; charset=utf-8` when the payload contains rich `blocks` JSON (JSON bodies are required for `files.upload_v2`). GET with query parameters also works on read endpoints.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C1234567890", "text": "Hello from an agent"}'
```

Always inspect the JSON result:

- `{"ok": true, ...}` — success; use returned IDs (`ts`, `channel`, `file.id`) for follow-ups.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "invalid_auth"}` — token invalid; stop and report.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "not_in_channel"}` — bot must join the channel first via `conversations.join`.
- `{"ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found"}` — the channel argument was not a valid channel ID.
- HTTP 429 with `{"ok": false, "error": "rate_limited"}` — wait for the `Retry-After` header seconds and retry once.

## Resolving IDs

Endpoints expect IDs, not display names. `#general` or `general` will fail on most endpoints. Resolve first:

- **Channel ID from name**: `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel` and `limit=200`, paginating with `cursor`, then match `name` or `name_normalized`. `channels.list` and `groups.list` are legacy aliases.
- **User ID from email**: `users.lookupByEmail` with `email=...` returns `user.id`.
- **User ID from name**: `users.list` (paginate with `cursor`) and match `name` or `profile.display_name`.

## Sending and Managing Messages

### Post a message

`chat.postMessage` with `channel` (channel, user, or conversation ID), `text`, and optional `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `username`/`icon_emoji` (bot tokens only), and `link_names`.

### Reply in a thread

Pass `thread_ts` equal to the parent message's `ts`. Replies without `thread_ts` start new messages. To fetch a thread, use `conversations.replies` with `channel` and `ts`.

### Update and delete

- `chat.update` — requires `channel` and `ts` of the original message; supports `text` and `blocks`.
- `chat.delete` — requires `channel` and `ts`. Deletes are irreversible; prefer `chat.postMessage` with a corrective message if unsure.
- `chat.postEphemeral` — send a message only a specific user sees (`user` field required).

## Reading Conversations

- `conversations.history` — fetch messages from a channel with `channel`, `limit` (1–999), `oldest`/`latest` (Unix timestamps or `ts` values), and `inclusive`.
- `conversations.replies` — fetch a thread by `channel` + `ts`.
- `conversations.info` — metadata for one channel.
- `conversations.members` — list member user IDs of a channel.

Paginate every list-style call: when `response_metadata.next_cursor` is non-empty, repeat the call adding `cursor=<next_cursor>`. Do not assume `limit` returns everything.

## Users and Presence

- `users.info` with `user` — profile, timezone, status, and `is_bot`.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — fastest way to get a user ID.
- `users.list` — all workspace users; paginate.
- `users.getPresence` with `user` — `active`/`away` presence.

## Uploading Files

- `files.upload_v2` (preferred) with `channel_id`, `content` or `file`/`filename`/`filetype`, and optional `initial_comment`. Returns `file.id`; the file appears in the channel when `channel_id` is supplied.
- `files.upload` (legacy) — for a single channel; JSON body required.
- `files.sharedPublicURL` — generate a public link for a file that already has `permalink_public` enabled.

## Searching

- `search.messages` with `query` — returns matching messages plus `permalink` and channel/thread context.
- `search.files` with `query` — returns matching files.
- Query syntax supports `from:@user`, `in:#channel`, `before:/after:` datestamps, and quoted phrases.
- User-token scopes (`search:read`) are required; bot tokens cannot search by default.

## Message Formatting

- **mrkdwn** in `text`: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `~strike~`, `<https://example.com|Link text>`, `@user`, `#channel`. Escape literal `&`, `<`, `>`.
- **Blocks**: `blocks` (JSON array) renders a rich layout (section, header, divider, context, actions) and is the recommended way to compose professional messages. When `blocks` is present, also provide a plain-text `text` fallback for notifications and accessibility.
- Line breaks in `text` are honored; use `\n` in JSON strings.

## Recommended Workflow
